## Positivity-limiter meters: `limcut`, `thetamin`, `thetasevere` (`_positivity_severe`) {#sec-ch13-limiter-meters}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Counts, over the whole run, how hard the species flux-positivity limiter of @sec-ch08 had to
act. It records the smallest limiter factor, the number of severe cuts and the fraction of the offered $x_1$
species flux that was cut. All three are printed in the run-to-date group of the cycle line (@sec-ch13-cycle).
**Switch.** `equation-of-state/limiter` (default false), and the run must carry species.
**Order.** Not a discretisation.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch13-limiter-severe.
:::

The limiter scales each species flux leaving a cell by a factor $\theta \in [0,1]$, so that the cell cannot be
drained below zero in a stage. The meters turn those factors into three numbers a reader can watch. `thetamin=`
is the smallest $\theta$ so far. `thetasevere=` counts the (cell, species) entries cut hard enough to matter.
`limcut=` is the fraction of the offered $x_1$ flux that was cut.

### Derivation

For a species of density $\rho_y$ in cell $i$, with $D_i$ the mass its faces would remove in the stage step
$\Delta t$, the limiter factor is
$\theta_i = \min\big(1, (1-4096\epsilon)\,\rho_{y,i}V_i/D_i\big)$ where $D_i > 0$, and 1 elsewhere. The mass held
back is $(1-\theta_i)D_i$. An entry is severe when

$$
\theta_i < 0.9 \quad\text{and}\quad (1-\theta_i)\,D_i > n_{\mathrm{ulp}}\,\epsilon\,m_i ,
$$ {#eq-ch13-limiter-severe}

with $m_i$ the cell's gas mass, dry plus all species, and $n_{\mathrm{ulp}} = 4096$ in float64 or 64 in float32.
The second condition keeps round-off events out of the count. The thresholds are $9.09\times10^{-13}$ and
$7.63\times10^{-6}$ of the gas mass [check `src/snapy_report/ch13/limiter_meters_check.py`, output
`limiter_meters_check.out`, `[C3]`].

On a settling column where $\Delta t\,|v_{\mathrm{sed}}|/\Delta x = 2$ in five draining cells, $\theta$ is
$1/2$ in those cells. That gives five hits, five severe entries, `thetamin` $1/2$ and `limcut` $1/2$, each to
$5\times10^{-13}$, the size of the $4096\epsilon$ margin (`[C1]`). An empty cell drained by a $10^{-20}$ face flux
has $\theta = 0$ and counts as a hit, but not as severe (`[C2]`). When the limiter never cuts, `thetamin` stays at
its initial 1, `thetasevere` at 0, and `limcut` is not printed (`[C4]`).

In the code, @eq-ch13-limiter-severe is the census into `_positivity_severe`
([`hydro_forward.cpp:656-669`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L656-L669)).

### Numerical method

See @fig-ch13-limiter-meters for the settling column of the check.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch13-limiter-meters
#| fig-cap: "The settling column of the check. Left: the limiter factor $\\theta$ of each cell; the five draining cells have $\\theta=1/2$, below the severe threshold 0.9 (vermillion). Right: the offered $|F|$ of each face (orange) and the part the limiter cut (vermillion); limcut is the sum of the cuts over the sum of the offers, here 1/2."
#| fig-alt: "Two bar charts: theta per cell, one bar at 1 and five at 0.5 under a dashed line at 0.9; and paired offered and cut flux bars on five faces, the cut bars half the offered ones."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch13.fig_limiter_meters import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The factor comes from `flux_positivity_theta`, with the margin `margin` of 4096 ulp in every precision
([`flux_positivity.cpp:61-71`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp#L61-L71)). The round-off bound of the severe test is `positivity_roundoff`, from the
two constants `kPositivityRoundoffUlp` and `kPositivityRoundoffUlpFloat` ([`flux_positivity.hpp:18-23`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/flux_positivity.hpp#L18-L23)).
In each stage, `HydroImpl::forward` takes a census of the interior entries before the ghost fill. It adds the
entries with $\theta<1$ to `_positivity_hits`, the severe ones to `_positivity_severe`, and lowers
`_positivity_min` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:656-669`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L656-L669)). After the fluxes are scaled, it adds the offered
interior $x_1$ flux magnitude to `_lim_flux` and the cut to `_lim_cut` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:690-705`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L690-L705)).

The five meters are module buffers set up with `register_buffer` at construction: 0 for the counts and sums, 1
for the minimum ([`hydro/hydro.cpp:187-194`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L187-L194)). The cycle line sums the counts and the two flux totals over
blocks and ranks, takes the MIN of $\theta$, and prints the ratio only when the offered total is positive, through
`limcut` ([`meshblock.cpp:1102-1107`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1102-L1107)). The hit count is not printed. It is read by the step acceptance
(@sec-ch07-redo) through the EOS limiter marks, `limiter_hits` ([`meshblock.cpp:1212-1218`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1212-L1218)).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
`limcut` measures the $x_1$ flux only. A run whose limiter acts in $x_2$ or $x_3$ shows it in `thetamin` and
`thetasevere`, not in `limcut`.
:::

1. **Initial values.** A run whose limiter never cut prints `thetamin=1` and `thetasevere=0`. That reads as "no
   cut", not as "meter off" (#217 Limits, `sources/gh__PR_BODIES_202-219.md`).
2. **Run to date.** The meters are never reset during a run, so a single bad step stays in `thetamin` for the
   rest of the run.
3. **Scalars.** The passive-scalar module keeps its own hit counter, `_positivity_hits`
   ([`scalar.cpp:160`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/scalar/scalar.cpp#L160)), which is not printed.
